questions: What is Quant·ion?
What is quantion for?
How does quantion work?
What can quantion do?
Why should I use quantion?
What's quantion helpful for?
items.answer: Quant·ion is an LC-MS pipeline for `targeted` and `untargeted` feature detection and quantification. It reads Ionic (.ion) and mzML files, builds chromatograms, and measures noise, baseline and peaks. One Rust core gives the same results in Rust, Python, JavaScript and R.

questions: How do I get peaks above 1000 intensity?
Keep only peaks higher than 500
Peaks over an intensity of 2000
How do I remove small peaks?
Set a minimum intensity for peaks
items.answer: To keep only peaks above {value}, set `min_intensity` = {value} in the function that fits your data: `find_peaks` for every peak in a trace, `get_peak` for one peak at a known rt, `find_features` for `untargeted` peaks in one file, and `match_features` to match features across samples.
items.answerWithout: To keep only bigger peaks, set `min_intensity` in the function that fits your data: `find_peaks` for every peak in a trace, `get_peak` for one peak at a known rt, `find_features` for `untargeted` peaks in one file, and `match_features` to match features across samples.

questions: What are mz and rt?
What do mz and rt mean?
What is the difference between m/z and retention time?
Explain mz and rt
items.answer: `mz` is the m/z of the ion you look for. It usually comes from the monoisotopic mass, and it differs between positive and negative ion mode. `rt` is when the compound comes off the column, in minutes. An `mz` plus an `rt` is what lets Quant·ion find and measure one compound.

questions: I know my compounds
I know which compounds I look for
How does targeted analysis work?
How do I quantify known compounds?
How do I measure the compounds in my list?
items.answer: `Targeted` means you know what you look for. A target is `{ id, mz, rt }`, plus an optional `range`. Many compounds in one file: `find_targets` builds each EIC and finds each peak. SRM or MRM data (Q1, Q3): `find_transitions`. One known compound in a trace you already have: `get_peak` at its `rt`. Every peak in a trace: `find_peaks`. Peak shape (width, tailing): `fit_peak`.

Name my features
How do I identify my features?

items.answer: Use `annotate_features`: it matches the MS2 spectrum of each feature against a spectral library and gives it a name and a score. Once you know the names, make them targets and quantify them with `find_targets`.

questions: My retention times shift between runs
The peaks move between samples, what can I do?
How do I handle retention time drift?
How do I predict where my targets elute in a new sample?
items.answer: Retention times can shift from run to run. `calibrate` turns the rt seen in anchor samples (LTRs, QCs) into targets, and `predict_rts` predicts where each target elutes in a new sample. Both are experimental.
